newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TransAlta NZ pledges to hold electricity prices.
newsitem.headline: TransAlta NZ pledges to hold electricity prices.

text.p: TransAlta NZ, the new company to be formed from the merger of EnergyDirect and Wellington's Capital Power, pledged on Tuesday to hold electricity prices for two years for residential and small business customers.
The pledge and the new contracts mean that the financial forecasts included in the Listing Profile sent to EnergyDirect shareholders last week will be updated.
TransAlta NZ chairman Ron Arbuckle said the price pledge was the first tangible evidence of the company's promise to share the merger benefits with customers.
TransAlta Corp of Canada owns 41 percent of EDL and all of Capital Power, and will control 63 percent of the merged company.
Arbuckle said the price pledge was subject to certain conditions which are expected to be satisfied.
These include contracts with national grid operator Trans Power coming into and remaining in effect, and significant swings in generation prices being avoided, he said.

"Directors of TransAlta NZ have stated that merger benefits would be shared with our customers. We have selected the price pledge as our way of doing this, because our customers have told us that they are concerned about rising prices and they value price certainty."
TransAlta NZ was also considering pricing initiatives that would be beneficial for large industrial and commercial customers.
The EnergyDirect board also reported that EnergyDirect had successfully negotiated and signed a new contract with Trans Power NZ, resulting in lower transmission costs.
Capital Power has signed a similar contract.

"The net result of these contracts is that customers will receive merger benefits through a price pledge and shareholders of TransAlta NZ will receive benefits through increased dividends," Arbuckle said.

The updated financial forecasts will be posted to EnergyDirect shareholders on Wednesday. Shareholders of EnergyDirect and Capital Power will vote on the merger proposal next Monday and it will take effect on October 1 if approved.
